simulator.note: Draws its installation wizard "Welcome" (Region, Language, Display Mode 576i, Aspect Mode Auto, OK) at ~315 M instructions, 91 GE commands; DOWN moves its highlight (run_dump_t50_capture_screen.py, 2026-10-14).  Its OSD is drawn by the M3602's own GE at 0xB800C000 (ge_m3602.py, the SDK's ge_hal.c) into a 912 x 640 CLUT8 screen, which the GE scales through the YCbCr palette into the 513 x 512 AYCbCr8888 layer of its PAL output (layer 1: 0xB80061A0 bit 8, head at 0xB80061AC).  On the way: its video output driver polled the output's status bit 0 (0xB8006004 bit 8) before switching TV systems (video_m36 sets it half a field after each field start); its control task then waited on libpub's event flag for its logo, whose PUB task polls the decoder's VDEC_CB_FIRST_SHOWED callback -- which its decoder, in the dual-output mode (+0xB44 = 8), calls only once the SD output (the DEO at 0xB8020000, interrupt-controller line 15, its field at bit 19) has requested the frame too.  Its remote key table (0x802F2DC4, 63 entries) holds each key's command half only, rev8(command) << 8 | rev8(~command); its control task drops a key unless the received code's high half is 0x803F (0x8000AD0C): extended NEC with the address bytes 0x01, 0xFC (ir_remote coding "cmd").  The M3101 demodulators at I2C 0x20 / 0x21 and the tuner it asks for at 0x63 still do not answer.  Before: with the flash's electronic ID answered as a real 4 MB part answers it (2026-10-13: the last byte of the 0xAB read, 0x15 -- the 2009 bootloader's flash table knows the part by that byte only) its flash driver attaches the flash and the bootloader starts the application: "MC: APP  init ok", Libcore 1.1.6@Auto_20100413, the demultiplexer's and the video decoders' attach messages; it then sets up its two M3101 demodulators at I2C 0x20 / 0x21 and asks for an MxL5007T-type tuner at 0x63 behind them -- nothing answers there -- and polls the first demodulator's lock register; no GE command within 230 M instructions.  Its AppInit completes at ~29 M (it returns at 0x8001D544), but the UI's control task never reaches its key loop (get_key, 0x800099C0, not called after 60 M): no remote frame reaches its key lookup (0x80008C6C), whatever the address, and stand-in demodulators at 0x20 / 0x21 change nothing.  Its key table (0x802F2DC4, 63 entries) is the older layout: each code is the low half of the received NEC code, rev8(command) << 8 | rev8(~command), without the address byte (ir_remote.find_key_table then wanted one shared address byte).  Its video output's interrupt looks up the OSD drivers "OSD_M3327C_0", "OSD_M3327C_1" and "OSD_M3327_0" every field, but no OSD layer is set up in any display block (0xB8006000, 0xB800E000, 0xB8020000) by 120 M.  Before: As the M3602 family (chip ID 0x3602, 2026-10-10): the bootloader prints "APP  init ok" 459 times in 100 M instructions and starts over each time without starting the application.

desc: Ferguson Ariva T50 firmware V1.02B214, the manufacturer's USB update image from Ferguson's download area (ArivaT50_20111118_V102B214.zip).

Despite the .abs name it is a complete flash image: the ALi chunk chain from offset 0 -- bootloader 0x000000 (DMB01---0.1.0, 2011-11-18), maincode 0x010000 (Demo M3602, 2011-11-18), radioback 0x340000 (1.0.0, 2010-6-25), bootlogo 0x348000 (1.0.0, 2010-6-21), customerradiolo 0x358000 (1.0.0, 2011-8-16), countryband 0x360000 (1.1.0, 2011-11-18), userdb 0x36FF80 (1.0.0, 2011-11-18); the maincode's CRC-32/MPEG-2 is intact.  Banners in its LZMA streams: Libcore version 1.1.6@Auto_20100413.
The front-panel driver is "PAN_PT_0" (a PT6964-style shift-register panel in ALi's SDK), not one front_panel.py decodes yet.

The bootloader chunk's version is "DMB01---0.1.0" (its Libcore 1.0.9@Auto_20090520); the chain also carries a boot logo ("bootlogo", an MPEG still) and a "customerradiolo" (the radio-mode background).
The simulator runs it as the M3602 family (chips/m3602.py).

In the simulator (2026-10-10, the M3602 family): the bootloader probes its DDR at 0xA800AA68 (the family shows the RAM again above 128 MB), prints "APP  init ok", identifies the flash (JEDEC EF 40 16), reads it and runs a bitwise CRC (MIPS16 code at 0x806842EA in its RAM copy), and then takes its reset path: $fp = 0xDEADBEAD and the routine at 0x80688C34, which pulses the module resets (0xB8000080 = 0xFFBFFFFF for chip 0x3602; 0x1FF to 0xB8000060 for any other chip ID) and jumps to 0xBFC00000.  The path that starts the application instead sets $fp = 0xDEADBEEF and jumps to the flash entry 0xAFC00000 (0x80688D5C), whose reset code checks for that value.  It was not a failed check: the bitwise loop is the CRC table's set-up, and check_program's first flash read (sto_fetch_long, 0x806845D8) found no flash device and called that reset routine (0x80688D48) -- the flash driver's attach had registered none, as no entry of its table matched the part's IDs (2026-10-13).
